catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 publishes joint positions in rad and has no absolute XYZ micrometre input, while the stage is addressed in micrometres (PositionerController.py:23-26) and its coordinated move takes an (x, y, z) tuple with axis='XYZ' (ESP32StageManager.py:534-541); cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 binds robot.arm only, not motion.axis. The extension carries the native unit without inventing a radian conversion.
catalogue_requests.summary: Move the X, Y and Z stage axes to absolute positions in micrometres with the upstream coordinated XYZ move.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/openuc2__imswitch --backend fake` on 2026-11-05 with digest sha256:27131cf05993d6caf5ddafb16fda94e77340719631eb5d1a756c239942103454; check-report.json has no findings and no warnings. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run helper-wave-2-002), reviewed_by is null, and no human reviewed or tested anything here. No hardware was attached, the hardware backend (native.py) was never opened, and no MHS-Device level is claimed: evidence is contract_checked. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper, but the package is a direct Driver; the coordinated XYZ move needs axis='XYZ', is_absolute=True and is_blocking=True plus an (x, y, z) tuple (ESP32StageManager.py:534-541), which that helper's one-call command table cannot build. The card's decision direct-driver is retained. The card's preferred upstream-sim is not available: MockXXInfo is an empty setup-info dataclass (SetupInfo.py:348), MockPositionerManager has a different move/get_position surface (MockPositionerManager.py:22-30), and VirtualStageManager is a separate manager that drives a VirtualMicroscope (VirtualStageManager.py:6-38 and 48-66); the package therefore ships an in-memory fake at the ESP32 manager's method level. Interface: reads x_um, y_um and z_um in micrometres from getPosition(); x-cap.openuc2.move_xyz.v1 calls the native coordinated move and reports the position read back; cap.motion.stop.v1 is the safe-state action and calls stopAll(); @estop calls stopAll() (native stopAll). Limits: the three move inputs are Limit.operator_required because no text of the clone states the travel of an installed stage (the manager reads minX/maxX, minY/maxY and minZ/maxZ from the positioner setup with -inf/inf defaults, ESP32StageManager.py:62-76, and the combined XYZ branch checks no soft limit, lines 534-544); site-limits.example.json is an example-only 0 to 1000 um envelope, not a fact about a unit; hardware use is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies site-limits.json. Safety: R2; no independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so estop_physical_ref is unset and the non-empty safe_state.achieved_by (cap.motion.stop.v1) is the SAFE-045 route; this is a software stop, not an independent hardware stop. The upstream stop is one _motor.stop() through the same uc2rest motor object as the blocking move; the clone shows no queue drain, settling wait or lock order, and getPosition() falls back to its cached _position when the device query raises (ESP32StageManager.py:605-617); the driver therefore claims no quiescence and has no independent stopped-state evidence. The upstream constructor commands dummy moves and optional homing and pushes TMC, joystick and hard-limit settings to the controller (ESP32StageManager.py:250-333), so the hardware backend needs the human hardware review that the loader requires for an unreviewed model R2 package. Mock/fidelity: the fake completes moves at once; it models no motor time, acceleration, step loss, backlash, ESP32 serial protocol or firmware reply; its start positions are placeholders, it is not a recording, and no upstream simulator of this manager exists. Not covered: [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver over ESP32StageManager against the clone at the pin: every fact and the three operator_required travel limits with show_refs.py (the card's limit hints SetupInfo.py:317-326 are galvo DAC units, not stage travel), native.py line by line, the stop path, the fake, scope, provenance, licence and R2; the stop is source-backed, stopAll() -> _motor.stop() being the upstream's own immediate all-axis stop (PositionerController.py:739-746, UC2ConfigController.py:246-266, ESP32StageManager.py:1066-1075), and no @reset or re-enable exists. Defects: stopAll() returns nothing, yet cap.motion.stop.v1 returned stopped=true and the e-stop completed whenever the call returned, and getPosition() returns its cached _position, the last commanded target, when the device query raises (605-617, 542-544), so reads, the move output and stopped_position could report a commanded target as a measurement; a probe of a stage that keeps moving and of a failing query showed both (review/lists/hw2-openuc2-probe_stop_confirmation.py, -probe-output.txt). The reviewer changed driver.py (cached fallbacks refused: reads MHS.DEVICE.FAULTED, the move unknown, also when the native move raises; the safe-state stop confirms a standstill by two fresh device reads 0.2 s apart, else SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; teardown stops before closing, agents.md:893-896; safe_state rewritten; facts corrected, narrowed or added, 33 now, one having claimed a comparison outside its cited lines), native.py (options checked before any import; X, Y, Z and calibrated stepsizeX/Y/Z required, the upstream default being 1, 55-60; frameHomeOnStart refused, a background homing thread, 350-352, 988-992), fake.py (the upstream's fresh-dict, cached-object and position-property semantics, keeps_moving and query_fails switches), test_driver.py (three cases) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:27131cf05993d6caf5ddafb16fda94e77340719631eb5d1a756c239942103454); the author's notes that the stop action calls only stopAll() and that the driver has no stopped-state evidence are superseded. For the human reviewer: R2 motorised XYZ microscope stage (objective or sample collision; the clone lifts Z at least 3 mm before XY homing); the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs. The stop and every position read go through uc2rest (UC2-REST), outside the clone: confirm on the bench that _motor.stop() halts a move_xyz blocking in another thread (the upstream's own cancels assume it) and that get_position() queries the firmware rather than a uc2rest cache. If the stop waits behind the move, the e-stop ends unreached (timeout) with the latch held until the move returns (review/lists/hw2-openuc2-probe_running_move_estop.py). The standstill check needs two identical reads: a position that jitters at rest never confirms (latch held, retried), and a stage slower than one position step per 0.2 s would pass. A move cancelled by an e-stop reports cancelled after its native call returned; the stage may have moved part or all of the way. Connecting switches the motors on, makes a -1/+1 dummy move on every configured axis, homes when homeOnStart<axis> is set and pushes TMC, hard-limit and joystick settings; supply calibrated stepsizeX/Y/Z (the clone's example uses 0.396, 0.396, 0.3125 um/step) and the travel in site-limits.json. No independent hardware e-stop is documented for this stage; a UC2 CAN master can report a hardware E-stop button (UC2ConfigController.py:163-195), which a human may cite as estop_physical_ref if the rig has one. gTIMEOUT = 100 has no stated unit; a long move can outlast the caller's deadline and end unknown.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (fix) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. I found no blocker and no major issue. All 33 citations match their cited lines at the pin (show_refs.py reported 0 bad citations). collect.py --strict passes with exit 0, and the gate digest in RESULT.json is unchanged.

- **Stop:** stopAll() calls _motor.stop(), the upstream's own all-axis stop, and it is cited from three upstream callers. The driver now confirms a standstill with two fresh reads 0.2 s apart. A cached or failed read, or a position that still changes, ends SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held.
